title: Leray spectral sequence for a continuous map of spaces
statement: Let f:Z\to X be a continuous map of topological spaces [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], and let F be an abelian sheaf on Z. Let f_* be the direct-image functor on abelian sheaves given by (f_*F)(U)=F(f^{-1}U), a left exact additive functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive] from abelian sheaves on Z to abelian sheaves on X, and let R^qf_* be its right derived functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Then there are functorial first-quadrant cohomological spectral-sequence pages (E_r^{a,b},d_r)_{r>=2}, with d_r:E_r^{a,b}\to E_r^{a+r,b-r+1}, d_r\circ d_r=0, and E_{r+1}^{a,b}\cong ker(d_r:E_r^{a,b}\to E_r^{a+r,b-r+1})/im(d_r:E_r^{a-r,b+r-1}\to E_r^{a,b}). They satisfy E_2^{a,b}=H^a(X,R^bf_*F) for a,b>=0 and E_2^{a,b}=0 otherwise. For each n>=0, they converge to H^n(Z,F) in the sense that there is a finite decreasing filtration [def-sp-filtration] H^n(Z,F)=F^0H^n\supseteq F^1H^n\supseteq\cdots\supseteq F^{n+1}H^n=0 with F^aH^n/F^{a+1}H^n\cong E_\infty^{a,n-a}, where E_\infty^{a,b}=E_r^{a,b} for all sufficiently large r. The pages, differentials, filtrations, and these identifications are functorial in F. Its edge map E_2^{p,0}=H^p(X,f_*F)\to E_\infty^{p,0}=F^pH^p(Z,F)\subseteq H^p(Z,F) is the Leray edge map; it is the map induced by f.

proof.text: Let Ab(Z) and Ab(X) denote the abelian categories of abelian sheaves on the two spaces. By the definition of topological sheaf cohomology, these categories have enough injectives, and H^a(X,-) is the right derived functor R^aΓ(X,-) of the left exact additive global-sections functor. The direct image f_* is left exact and additive because it is computed sectionwise by (f_*G)(U)=G(f^{-1}U).

source.place: Section 01DZ (cohomology of abelian sheaves on a topological space) and Lemma 01F2 (cohomology-lemma-Leray)

proof.text: The new injective-pushforward lemma says that f_* sends injectives to injectives. Applying the general acyclicity clause for derived functors to the left exact additive functor Γ(X,-), every f_*I with I injective is Γ(X,-)-acyclic, so f_* sends injectives to Γ(X,-)-acyclics [def-sp-acyclic]. Moreover Ab(Z) and Ab(X) are Grothendieck abelian: an abelian sheaf on a space is the same as a sheaf of modules over the constant sheaf of rings Z on the small site of open subsets, so the Grothendieck-abelian clause of [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] applies. Hence (f_*,Γ(X,-)) is a composable pair [def-sp-composite-acyclicity] with f_* sending injectives to Γ(X,-)-acyclics, which is the hypothesis of the Grothendieck spectral-sequence theorem.

The Grothendieck spectral-sequence theorem applied to F=f_* and G=Γ(X,-) gives a functorial first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequence with E_2^{a,b}=R^aΓ(X,R^bf_*F)=H^a(X,R^bf_*F), converging to R^{a+b}(Γ(X,-)∘f_*)F. Since Γ(X,f_*G)=Γ(Z,G) sectionwise, the composite is Γ(Z,-), so its derived functors are H^{a+b}(Z,F).

The construction clause of [thm-sp-grothendieck] identifies the Leray spectral sequence with the second spectral sequence of the double complex Γ(X,I^{•,•}) of [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences], and the spectral-sequence structure [def-sp-spectral-sequence] identifies the pages and differentials as d_r:E_r^{a,b}\to E_r^{a+r,b-r+1} with d_r\circ d_r=0 and E_{r+1}^{a,b}=ker(d_r)/im(d_r), and its first-quadrant convergence gives E_2^{a,b}=0 outside a,b>=0, stabilization E_∞^{a,b}=E_r^{a,b} for all sufficiently large r, and a finite decreasing filtration F^0H^n=H^n⊇...⊇F^{n+1}H^n=0 with F^aH^n/F^{a+1}H^n≅E_∞^{a,n-a}. The construction is functorial in F. The bottom edge is the map R^pΓ(X,f_*F)=H^p(X,f_*F) to the abutment induced by the composite Γ(X,f_*F)=Γ(Z,F), hence is the map induced by f.
